classification.difficultyReason: Translate capacity and strict profit requirements into simultaneous inequalities, account for whole-item quantities, and describe feasible production without assuming that all 70 items must be made.

content.prompt: A small business produces handmade candles and soaps. Each candle brings in $\$7$ profit and each soap brings in $\$5$ profit. Time constraints mean at most 70 items can be produced each week. If the profit must exceed $\$450$, write a statement about how many candles and soaps will suit the requirements.

answer.short:
Let $c$ and $s$ be the numbers of candles and soaps. Produce non-negative integer quantities satisfying $c+s\leq70$ and $7c+5s>450$.

If exactly 70 items are made, produce 51–70 candles and make up the remainder with soaps.
answer.worked:
Let $c$ be the number of candles and $s$ the number of soaps. The requirements are
$$\begin{align*}c+s&\leq70\\7c+5s&>450\end{align*}$$
where $c$ and $s$ are non-negative integers.

If exactly 70 items are produced, $s=70-c$, so
$$\begin{align*}7c+5(70-c)&>450\\2c+350&>450\\2c&>100\\c&>50.\end{align*}$$
Thus 51–70 candles, with soaps making the total 70, meet the requirements. If fewer than 70 items are produced, both original inequalities must still hold.
